title: NanoAmpli-Seq - Bioinformatics Workflow
author: Szymon T STC Calus
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.u25eyg6
materials: Identification of segments made of 16S rRNA genes.
Optimal read sections are used for clustering.

steps.title: Configure System Environment Paths
steps.instruction: Export the necessary PATHs for the required programs to ensure the software tools are accessible in the terminal.

steps.title: Basecall Raw Data
steps.instruction: Basecall raw HDF5 data generated with MinKNOW using Albacore v2.3.3 (or newer) software. Use the full_1dsq_basecaller.py algorithm to ensure only 1D2 data is produced in FASTA format.

substeps.instruction: Run command: /home/opt/.pyenv/versions/3.5.0/bin/full_1dsq_basecaller.py -i data/ -f FLO-MIN107 -k SQK-LSK308 -o fasta -t 20 -s .

steps.title: Perform Consensus Calling with INC-Seq
steps.instruction: Use INC-Seq to correct basecalled 1D2 FASTA data. This process identifies 16S rRNA gene segments and performs anchor alignment of concatamerised amplicons and consensus calling with PBDAGCon to achieve ~98% accuracy.

substeps.instruction: Run command: inc-seq.py -i input.fasta -a poa -o incseq.fasta --iterative --copy_num_thre 3

steps.title: Process Reads with chopSEQ
steps.instruction: Process INC-Seq corrected data using chopSEQ to identify primers, re-orient incorrectly concatamerised reads, remove tandem repeats (via etandem/EMBOSS), merge reads, and perform size filtration via Biopython.

steps.title: Perform OTU Binning with nanoCLUST
steps.instruction: Run nanoCLUST on chopSEQ corrected data to partition reads, group them by 97% similarity using VSEARCH, perform dereplication and singleton removal, and generate consensus sequences (~99.5% accuracy) and an abundance table using MAFFT G-INS-i for alignment.
